easy.def: A tool that makes your voice louder.
examples: The singer held the microphone.
I spoke into the microphone.
The microphone is on.

more.def: A device that picks up sound and sends it to speakers or a recorder.
examples: The speaker tapped the microphone to test it.
I spoke into the microphone at the assembly.
The microphone squealed.

easy.def: A tool that makes tiny things look big.
examples: I looked through the microscope.
The microscope shows tiny bugs.
We used a microscope in class.

more.def: A tool with lenses that makes very small things look much bigger so that you can see them clearly.
examples: We used a microscope to look at tiny creatures in a drop of pond water.
Through the microscope, a grain of salt looks like a clear block.
The scientist adjusted the microscope until the picture was sharp.

easy.def: An oven that heats food very fast.
examples: I put my soup in the microwave.
The microwave beeped.
Mom uses the microwave.

more.def: A small oven that cooks or warms food very quickly using waves of energy.
examples: I warmed my soup in the microwave for one minute.
The microwave beeped when the popcorn was done.
Do not put metal in the microwave.

easy.def: To heat food in an oven that works very fast.
examples: I microwave my lunch.
Dad microwaved the soup.
She microwaved a potato.

more.def: To heat food using waves of energy in a small oven.
examples: I microwaved the leftover pasta for lunch.
Dad microwaved a bowl of soup in two minutes.
She microwaved the potato until it was soft.

easy.def: The center of something.
examples: Stand in the middle.
The middle of the cake is soft.
He sat in the middle.

more.def: The part that is in the center, with equal parts around it.
examples: A line runs down the middle of the road.
She sat in the middle of the back seat.
The middle of the pizza was still hot.

easy.def: In the center.
examples: The middle seat is mine.
She is the middle child.
The middle one is mine.

more.def: Located between two ends or sides.
examples: My middle brother plays the drums.
The middle shelf holds the books.
Take the middle path through the woods.

easy.def: Twelve o'clock at night.
examples: The clock struck midnight.
I was fast asleep at midnight.
We stayed up until midnight on New Year's Eve.

more.def: Twelve o'clock at night, when one day ends and the next begins.
examples: The old clock chimed twelve times at midnight.
The campers watched the stars at midnight.
At midnight the date on the calendar changes.

easy.def: The middle of something.
examples: She stood in the midst of the kids.
We were in the midst of lunch.
In the midst of the forest.

more.def: The middle of something, or the time when something is going on.
examples: He stood in the midst of the crowd.
We were in the midst of lunch when the phone rang.
A deer stood in the midst of the quiet forest.

easy.def: In the middle of the way.
examples: We stopped midway.
The ball stopped midway.
He was midway up the hill.

more.def: In the middle, halfway between two places or times.
examples: We stopped midway to rest and have a snack.
The ball rolled midway down the hill and stopped.
Midway through the movie, the power went out.

easy.def: The part of a fair with games and rides.
examples: We played games on the midway.
The midway was loud.
Lights lit the midway.

more.def: The area at a fair or carnival where the games, rides and food stands are found.
examples: We played ring toss on the midway at the county fair.
The midway was full of lights, music and the smell of popcorn.
Rides lined both sides of the midway.

easy.def: Very strong.
examples: The mighty lion roared.
He is a mighty giant.
A mighty wind blew.

more.def: Very strong and powerful.
examples: The mighty river carried boats to the sea.
The knight swung his mighty sword in the old tale.
A mighty oak tree stood at the edge of the field.

easy.def: A very bad headache.
examples: My aunt has a migraine.
A migraine hurts a lot.
He lay down with a migraine.

more.def: A very painful headache that can make a person feel sick and bothered by bright lights.
examples: My aunt had a migraine and had to lie down in a dark room.
A migraine can make bright lights hurt your eyes.
He took medicine from the doctor when he got a migraine.

easy.def: To move to a new place when the season changes.
examples: Some birds migrate when it gets cold.
Whales migrate to warm water.
The geese migrate in the fall.

more.def: To travel from one place to another at certain times of year, as many animals do.
examples: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles to warmer places each fall.
Huge herds of zebras migrate to find fresh grass.
Some whales migrate thousands of miles every year.

easy.def: Gentle.
examples: The weather is mild.
The soup is mild.
A mild cold.

more.def: Not harsh or strong, gentle.
examples: The weather is mild in spring.
The salsa was mild, not spicy.
I had a mild cold.

easy.def: A long distance.
examples: We walked a mile.
The school is one mile away.
He ran a mile.

more.def: A unit for measuring distance, equal to 5,280 feet.
examples: The path around the lake is two miles long.
We hiked one mile before lunch.
A mile is about as long as seventeen football fields.

easy.def: How many miles a car has gone.
examples: The car has high mileage.
Check the mileage.
The mileage is low.

more.def: The number of miles that a car has traveled, or the number of miles it can go on a certain amount of fuel.
examples: The old car has high mileage, with over a hundred thousand miles.
This car gets good mileage and uses little gas.
Dad checked the mileage before we started the trip.

easy.def: About soldiers and armies.
examples: A military base.
He wore a military uniform.
The military band marched.

more.def: Having to do with soldiers, armies or war.
examples: The military band played in the parade.
Soldiers lined up in a military camp.
The military base is outside of town.

easy.def: A white drink that comes from cows.
examples: I drink milk.
Cows give milk.
The milk is cold.

more.def: A white liquid that comes from cows and other mammals, used as a drink and in food.
examples: I drink a glass of milk with breakfast.
Goat milk can be made into cheese.
The baby kitten drank its mother's milk.

easy.def: To get a drink from a cow.
examples: The farmer milks the cow.
She milks the goat.
He milked the cows.

more.def: To draw the white drink out of a cow or goat.
examples: The farmer milks the cows every morning.
She milked the goat before breakfast.
They milked the cow by hand.

easy.def: Like milk, white and cloudy.
examples: The milky water.
A milky tea.
The sky was milky.

more.def: White and cloudy like milk, or containing a lot of milk.
examples: The water in the pond looked milky and cloudy.
She drank a cup of milky tea.
The Milky Way is a band of stars that looks like spilled milk.

easy.def: A building where grain is made into flour.
examples: The mill grinds wheat.
The old mill is by the river.
The mill has a wheel.

more.def: A building with machinery where grain is ground into flour, or where goods are made.
examples: The old mill ground wheat into flour.
A water wheel turned at the mill.
The mill stood beside the stream.

easy.def: A time of one thousand years.
examples: A millennium is a thousand years.
The old temple is a millennium old.
The year 2000 began a new millennium.

more.def: A period of one thousand years.
examples: Many people celebrated the start of the new millennium in the year 2000.
The pyramids have stood for more than four millennia.
Scientists say it took a millennium for the glacier to form.

easy.def: A very, very small weight.
examples: A grain of salt is a milligram.
The pill has ten milligrams.
A milligram is very small.

more.def: A very small unit of weight, equal to one thousandth of a gram.
examples: The tablet contained five hundred milligrams of vitamin C.
A milligram is so small that you need a special scale to weigh it.
A grain of sand weighs about a milligram.

easy.def: A very small length, a thousandth of a meter.
examples: An ant is a few millimeters long.
A millimeter is tiny.
Measure in millimeters.

more.def: A very small unit of length, equal to one thousandth of a meter, about the thickness of a coin.
examples: The ant was only two millimeters long.
There are ten millimeters in one centimeter.
The rain gauge showed five millimeters of rain.

easy.def: A very big number: 1,000,000.
examples: A million stars are in the sky.
The city has a million people.
I wish I had a million toys.

more.def: The number 1,000,000, which is one thousand thousands.
examples: More than a million people live in the city.
The library has about a million books.
A million seconds is about eleven and a half days.

easy.def: A person who has a million dollars or more.
examples: The millionaire has a big house.
A millionaire gave money.
The millionaire is rich.

more.def: A very rich person who has at least a million dollars.
examples: The millionaire lived in a huge house.
A millionaire gave money to the hospital.
The millionaire bought a boat.

easy.def: The part of you that thinks and feels.
examples: Use your mind.
I changed my mind.
Keep it in mind.

more.def: The part of a person that thinks, remembers, and has ideas.
examples: A good puzzle gives your mind a workout.
She changed her mind and chose the blue one.
The song stayed in my mind all day.

easy.def: To be upset about something.
examples: I do not mind waiting.
Do you mind the noise?
She does not mind.

more.def: To be bothered or upset by something.
examples: I do not mind sharing my crayons with you.
Would you mind closing the window, please?
He minded the cold less than his brother did.

easy.def: A word for something that belongs to me.
examples: That book is mine.
The red cup is mine.
Is this one yours or mine?

more.def: A word used for something that belongs to the person who is speaking.
examples: I found a blue backpack, but it is not mine.
Your drawing is great, and mine is not as good.
The seat next to the window is mine.

easy.def: A person who digs coal or metal underground.
examples: The miner wore a helmet.
A miner digs for coal.
Miners work underground.

more.def: A person whose job is to dig for coal, metal or stone underground.
examples: The miner wore a helmet with a lamp.
Miners dig for coal underground.
The miner found gold.

easy.def: A hard material found in the earth, such as salt or gold.
examples: Salt is a mineral.
A diamond is a mineral.
The rock has minerals.

more.def: A natural material found in the earth that is not alive, such as salt, gold or quartz.
examples: Salt is a mineral that we use to flavor food.
The rock was made of several different minerals.
Our bodies need small amounts of minerals, such as iron and calcium.

easy.def: To mix with other people at a party.
examples: We mingle at the party.
The guests mingled.
She mingled with friends.

more.def: To move around and talk with different people at a party or event.
examples: Guests mingled and chatted at the party.
She mingled with the other parents at the school fair.
The sounds of music and laughter mingled in the air.

easy.def: Very small.
examples: We ate mini pizzas.
A mini car.
The mini golf course is fun.

more.def: Much smaller than usual.
examples: We ate mini pizzas for lunch.
A mini car squeezed into the tiny space.
We played mini golf on the summer afternoon.

easy.def: Very small.
examples: She has a miniature horse.
A miniature house.
The toy is miniature.

more.def: Much smaller than the usual size of a thing of its kind.
examples: She built a miniature house for her dolls out of cardboard.
A miniature horse is only about as tall as a large dog.
The museum had a miniature train that ran around the room.

easy.def: A very small copy of something.
examples: I have a miniature of the car.
The miniature was cute.
She made a miniature.

more.def: A very small copy or model of something, or a tiny painting.
examples: He collected miniatures of famous buildings, each small enough to hold.
The shop sold miniatures of old cars.
The artist painted a miniature of the tiny flower.

easy.def: The least amount.
examples: The minimum age is five.
Use the minimum of salt.
The minimum score is ten.

more.def: The smallest amount or number that is allowed or possible.
examples: The minimum age for the ride is five.
Add the minimum amount of water.
The test has a minimum of ten questions.

easy.def: Digging deep in the ground for gold or other things.
examples: Mining is hard work.
My uncle works in mining.
Mining gave the town jobs.

more.def: The work of digging coal, metals or other useful materials out of the ground.
examples: Mining for gold brought thousands of people to the area long ago.
Workers wear helmets with lamps for safety during mining.
Coal mining was the main job in the little town.

easy.def: A leader of a church.
examples: The minister gave a talk.
The minister said a prayer.
The minister greeted us.

more.def: A person who leads religious services in some churches.
examples: The minister gave a talk on Sunday morning.
The minister greeted everyone at the church door.
A minister led the prayers.

easy.def: A leader in some governments.
examples: She is a minister in the government.
The prime minister gave a speech.
He is the minister of education.

more.def: A person who is in charge of a part of a government.
examples: The minister of health spoke on the news.
The prime minister met other leaders.
She became the minister of education.

easy.def: A part of a government that takes care of one big job.
examples: The ministry of health helps people.
She works at the ministry.
The ministry made a rule.

more.def: A department of a government that is in charge of an important area, such as health or schools.
examples: The ministry of health sent out information about washing hands.
In some countries, a ministry runs the schools.
She works at the ministry of transport.

easy.def: A small furry animal with a long body that lives near water.
examples: A mink swam in the stream.
The mink is brown.
I saw a mink.

more.def: A small animal with a long body, short legs and soft dark fur that lives near water.
examples: A mink swam in the stream looking for fish.
The mink has thick brown fur and a long tail.
A mink slipped quietly into the water.

easy.def: Small and not important.
examples: It was a minor mistake.
The cut is minor.
A minor problem.

more.def: Small, or less important than other things.
examples: It was only a minor mistake.
The cut was minor and healed fast.
There were a few minor changes in the plan.

easy.def: A smaller part of a group.
examples: A minority voted no.
Only a minority agreed.
The minority was small.

more.def: The smaller part of a group, with fewer than half of the people or things.
examples: Only a minority of the class voted for the green team shirts.
The minority of votes went to the second choice.
Only a minority of the class voted to have the party on Friday.

easy.def: A plant with a fresh, cool taste.
examples: The mint is green.
I put mint in my tea.
The mint smells nice.

more.def: A plant with a cool, fresh taste and smell that is used to flavor food.
examples: I put fresh mint in my tea.
The mint grew wild in the garden.
The gum tastes like mint.

easy.def: A sweet candy with a cool taste.
examples: I ate a mint.
The mint is white.
I sucked on a mint.

more.def: A small, sweet candy that has a cool, fresh flavor.
examples: I ate a mint after dinner.
The waiter left a mint with the bill.
She sucked on a mint.

easy.def: Take away.
examples: Five minus two is three.
Ten minus four is six.
Seven minus one is six.

more.def: Used in math to show that one number is taken from another.
examples: Twelve minus five is seven.
Ten minus four equals six.
I subtracted and found that nine minus three is six.

easy.def: Sixty seconds of time.
examples: Wait one minute.
It takes a minute.
I will be there in a minute.

more.def: A short period of time that is sixty seconds, or one sixtieth of an hour.
examples: An hour has sixty minutes.
Please wait a minute while I find my coat.
The bus will come in about ten minutes.

easy.def: Something wonderful that seems impossible.
examples: It was a miracle.
The rescue was a miracle.
A miracle happened.

more.def: A wonderful event that seems impossible or that cannot be explained.
examples: It was a miracle that no one was hurt.
The rescue of the lost puppy felt like a miracle.
Doctors called her recovery a miracle.

easy.def: Wonderful and amazing, like a miracle.
examples: It was a miraculous escape.
A miraculous cure.
The miraculous story.

more.def: So wonderful or surprising that it seems like a miracle.
examples: The boy made a miraculous escape from the stuck elevator.
The farmers called the sudden rain miraculous.
The doctor said her recovery was miraculous.

easy.def: A glass you look into to see yourself.
examples: I brush my hair in the mirror.
The mirror is on the wall.
She made a funny face in the mirror.

more.def: A smooth, shiny piece of glass that shows a picture of whatever is in front of it.
examples: A driver checks the mirror before changing lanes.
The dancers watched their moves in the huge mirror.
Light bounces off a mirror and lights up the dark corner.

easy.def: Silly things that can cause a little trouble.
examples: The puppy got into mischief.
My kitten is full of mischief.
The kids got into mischief in the mud.

more.def: Playful behavior that causes trouble or annoys people.
examples: The twins were always up to some kind of mischief.
The monkey's mischief made the zookeeper laugh.
There was a look of mischief in her eyes.

easy.def: Very unhappy.
examples: I felt miserable with a cold.
The rain made us miserable.
He felt miserable.

more.def: Very unhappy or uncomfortable.
examples: The cold, rainy day made us miserable.
I felt miserable with a stuffy nose.
The miserable puppy shivered in the rain.

easy.def: Great unhappiness.
examples: The rain caused misery.
He was in misery.
The misery ended.

more.def: A state of great sadness or pain.
examples: The cold rain made the camping trip a misery.
She was in misery with a bad cold.
The kitten's misery ended when we found it.

easy.def: Bad luck.
examples: It was our misfortune to get lost.
Losing the key was a misfortune.
He had the misfortune of missing the bus.

more.def: Bad luck, or something bad that happens to you by chance.
examples: It was our misfortune to be caught in the rain without umbrellas.
The family had the misfortune of losing their house in a flood.
Breaking her leg just before the trip was a real misfortune.

easy.def: To put something where you cannot find it.
examples: I misplaced my keys.
She misplaced her glasses.
He misplaced his hat.

more.def: To put something in the wrong place and forget where it is.
examples: I misplaced my keys and could not find them.
She misplaced her glasses and looked all over.
He misplaced his hat at the park.

easy.def: To feel sad that someone is not here.
examples: I miss my friend.
She misses her mom.
We miss the old house.

more.def: To feel sad because someone or something is not with you.
examples: I miss my cousins when they go home after the holidays.
He missed his dog while he was at camp.
The children miss summer when winter comes.

easy.def: To not catch, hit, or get something.
examples: I miss the ball.
She missed the bus.
He missed a day of school.

more.def: To fail to hit, catch, reach, or be present for something.
examples: I missed the bus, so my dad drove me to school.
The player missed the ball and ran to get it.
Do not miss the show about space tonight.

easy.def: A rocket that can be aimed at something far away.
examples: The museum has an old missile.
The rocket looks like a missile.
The scientist studied the missile.

more.def: A flying weapon or rocket that is aimed at a faraway target.
examples: The museum has an old missile on display.
Scientists have developed missiles that can fly very far.
The missile was shaped like a long tube with fins.

easy.def: An important job someone is sent to do.
examples: The astronauts' mission is to go to space.
The dog's mission was to find the ball.
Our mission is to clean the park.

more.def: An important task that a person or group is sent to do.
examples: The mission of the spaceship was to explore Mars.
Our class has a mission to clean the park.
The rescue team completed its mission.

easy.def: A person who goes far away to teach a religion or help people.
examples: A missionary came to our church.
The missionary built a school.
She is a missionary.

more.def: A person sent by a religious group to another place to teach about their faith or to help people with things like schools or health care.
examples: A missionary visited our church to talk about her work in a faraway village.
The missionaries built a small clinic in the mountains.
He traveled as a missionary to help people with food and medicine.

easy.def: A light cloud of tiny water drops close to the ground.
examples: Mist covered the lake.
I saw mist in the morning.
We walked into the mist.

more.def: A thin cloud of tiny drops of water in the air near the ground.
examples: A soft mist covered the lake in the early morning.
We could barely see the trees through the mist.
The mist rose from the river as the sun came up.

easy.def: Something that is wrong.
examples: I made a mistake.
There is a mistake in my math.
An eraser fixes a mistake.

more.def: An action or answer that is not right.
examples: She found one mistake in her spelling test.
It was a mistake to leave the door open.
Everybody makes mistakes when they are learning something new.

easy.def: A polite word before a man's name.
examples: Mister Lee is my teacher.
Hello, Mister Brown.
Thank you, Mister Jones.

more.def: A polite title used before a man's name.
examples: Mister Garcia teaches our music class.
Thank you, Mister Lee, for the ride.
Mister Brown waved from his porch.

easy.def: A plant with white berries used at Christmas.
examples: They hung mistletoe.
Mistletoe has berries.
The mistletoe is green.

more.def: A plant with small green leaves and white berries that grows on trees and is hung up at Christmas.
examples: We hung a sprig of mistletoe over the doorway at Christmas.
Mistletoe grows on tree branches and has white berries.
The berries of the mistletoe are poisonous.

easy.def: To get the wrong idea about something.
examples: I misunderstood the rules.
She misunderstood me.
We misunderstood the sign.

more.def: To fail to understand what someone says or means.
examples: I misunderstood the directions and went the wrong way.
She misunderstood what he said.
They misunderstood the sign.

easy.def: When you get the wrong idea about something.
examples: It was a misunderstanding.
We had a misunderstanding.
The misunderstanding was cleared up.

more.def: A mistake in understanding what someone says or means.
examples: It was only a misunderstanding, and we laughed.
A misunderstanding made us go to the wrong room.
They cleared up the misunderstanding with a talk.

easy.def: A very tiny animal that is related to a spider.
examples: A mite is tiny.
Dust has mites.
A mite lives on plants.

more.def: A tiny animal like a spider, too small to see easily, that lives on plants, animals and in dust.
examples: A mite is so small you need a microscope to see it.
Dust mites live in carpets and beds.
The mites made tiny holes in the leaves.

easy.def: A big glove, like the kind used in baseball.
examples: I caught the ball in my mitt.
Put on your mitt.
His mitt is big.

more.def: A thick glove with no separate fingers, such as the kind used for catching a baseball or for handling hot pots.
examples: He caught the fly ball in his baseball mitt.
Mom used an oven mitt to take the hot dish out of the oven.
My new mitt is stiff, so I need to break it in.

easy.def: To stir things together.
examples: Mix the paint.
She mixed the batter.
He mixes the salad.

more.def: To stir or blend things together.
examples: Mix the flour and eggs in a bowl.
She mixed red and yellow paint to make orange.
He mixed the salad with a big spoon.

related.def: To mix again; a new mix of a song.

easy.def: Two or more things mixed together.
examples: The cake mixture is ready.
A mixture of paint colors.
Sand and water make a mixture.

more.def: Something that is made by mixing different things together, so that each thing can still be told apart or separated.
examples: We stirred the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth mixture.
Trail mix is a mixture of nuts, raisins and cereal.
The mixture of sand and water was easy to separate by pouring it through a strainer.
